controls.cap_add: cap_drop: [ALL] stays; the listed capabilities are added back by name
controls.user: the image's own entrypoint keeps running as root and drops privileges itself; no user: line is written

exceptions.reason: mongo:3.4 generates its TLS certificate under /etc/ssl at start-up, chowns it and the data directory, then drops to mongodb with gosu (same sequence as the upstream compose file, with CN=mongo instead of the loopback alias).

The official postgres entrypoint starts as root, fixes ownership of the data directory (bind-mounted under runtime/volumes/), runs the init scripts, then drops to the postgres user with gosu. A fixed user: breaks first start on Linux hosts where the bind mount is owned by the developer.
exceptions.target: M5 (postgres:18 adopted by ADR-12; the entrypoint still starts as root, so the exception stays until the data volume is pre-created for uid 999)

exceptions.reason: The rabbitmq image writes its generated configuration and cookie under /etc/rabbitmq and /var/lib/rabbitmq as root before dropping to the rabbitmq user.
exceptions.target: M5 (current stable with RABBITMQ_CONFIG_FILE on a volume)

exceptions.reason: Apache httpd and shibd on the CentOS-based image start as root and bind ports 80/443.
Bundled test IdP (Java) writes its configuration at first start and runs as root in the current image.

One-shot owner step for every writable bind volume, replacing the per-volume elasticsearch_data_init and wiki_static_init: a fresh directory under runtime/volumes/ belongs to the host user, so a non-root writer (redis uid 999, the others 1000) cannot use it on a Linux or WSL2 host whose uid differs. Runs the postgres image, which every profile has, as explicit root (template run_as 0:0) with cap_drop ALL and only CAP_CHOWN, chowns each volume to the user: of its writers, then exits (restart: no); with only CAP_CHOWN it reaches another uid's private directory by taking ownership of it first (SPEC-02 §4); read_only and no-new-privileges stay. On Docker Desktop for Mac chown is a no-op.
exceptions.target: M4 (volume provisioning step in the installer, or Docker volume ownership options once the minimum Docker version allows)

note: Per-service exceptions to SPEC-03 §3.3 (non-root user, read-only root, cap_drop ALL). Every entry names the controls it relaxes, why, and when it is reviewed. privileged: true and no-new-privileges are never relaxed.
